note: Draft register for Spec 055 (design D-15, PR #195 packet), opened 2026-10-21 under the runnable-experiments campaign plan approved by the owner AS WRITTEN the same date (campaign member 11; decision E-7 recorded at F055-C09). Conventions as in Specs 032–046: requirement claims carry no falsification test where a gate or inspection is the operative check; boundaries carry the conditions under which each claim holds; evidence items carry observed_at from this draft because the cited facts were verified first-hand at drafting. The AEE lifecycle hooks have NOT run on this register; they are the freeze gate (tasks L4), and any recovery round they force changes claim text before any freeze digest is computed. ASM- ids name the assumptions each claim stands on: ASM-DESIGN-D15 (design D-15 as read in the PR #195 packet governs the substance), ASM-RECORD-AS-STATED (the claim record and Phase-104 evaluation state what this draft quotes them as stating), ASM-DOCUMENT-AS-SOURCE (the held cleaned text is the source document of record for the recovery), ASM-CORPUS-AS-PINNED (behaviour quantities are statements about the strict-corpus layer as identified and pinned at gate 0.4, and no other layer), ASM-GATES-BEFORE-OUTCOME (integrity, identification, and census precede any outcome quantity), ASM-APPEND-ONLY (outcomes append; frozen records are never edited), ASM-CAMPAIGN-E7 (campaign decision E-7: D-16 does not join this campaign even if this spec's recovery unblocks it). FREEZE RECOVERY (2026-10-21): normalised to engine evidence values at 0.6-draft (kind observed, source_quality artifact; refs, descriptions, observed_at unchanged — the draft's free-form labels are not engine values); at 0.7-draft the 14 irreducibility-challenged claim texts (all except F055-C01) were restated as single head propositions with carried clauses moved into boundaries verbatim-in-substance, and every multi-item claim's evidence gained mutual independent_of declarations. Freeze rulings DD-055-10 to DD-055-16 were carried into F055-C05, C08, C10, C11, C12, C13 before the hooks ran.

claims.text: An outcome under Spec 055 states only whether the sign identified from the fragment 'sign 900 means six' behaves as a numeral sign behaves, in the pinned strict corpus, under the frozen measures of spec §5.
claims.boundary: The scope is the two-stage question of design D-15: identification of one drawn sign from one held source document, then a behaviour comparison on one pinned corpus layer. It excludes any statement that the sign's value is six, any statement about what any sign means beyond the numeral question, any other corpus or population, and any finding about sign 700 or design D-16.
alternatives: the fragment could be read as already stating a finding about a known sign (it cannot: its record names no sign list and no drawn sign)
falsification_tests: the claim is falsified in scope if any Spec 055 output states a conclusion about a value, a meaning, a corpus, or a claim outside the identification and numeral-behaviour of this one sign

metadata.strongest_rival: the alternative reading in which identifying the sign, or passing the behaviour test, settles the value six
metadata.verdict_rule: scope is judged by inspection of every Spec 055 output against this boundary; any output exceeding it is a defect of the output, recorded as such, not a finding

claims.text: The falsifier of Spec 055 is two-stage.
claims.boundary: IDENTIFICATION FAILED is a pre-registered outcome about the source document and the record; it asserts nothing about the value six and nothing about the sign. The behaviour stage arises only on a successful identification; no behaviour wording may be attached to an identification closure. Carried from the draft text: the source document does not identify the sign — its list cannot be named from the document's own text, or the drawn sign its number 900 labels cannot be matched — closing as IDENTIFICATION FAILED; identification having succeeded, the identified sign's behaviour contradicts the numeral reading under spec §5.3.

claims.text: Execution stops before any identification if an input pin mismatches.
claims.boundary: These are spec §3's gates 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4. Their failure classes are CLOSED AT STEP 0 (pin mismatch, source not producible, corpus not pinnable) and IDENTIFIED — TOO FEW OCCURRENCES TO TEST (absent or below floor, count named). No failure is repaired at run time; a repaired input is a new freeze, not a resumed run. The occurrence floor is this draft's addition (DD-055-4), flagged OPEN-3 for the freeze. Ruled at the freeze (DD-055-13): the strict-corpus pinning posture is confirmed as drafted — the layer is a database posture (the Spec 048 precedent for the same layer), identified, exported and pinned by SHA-256 at execution gate 0.4 before any counting, and no file pin is stated at this freeze, because no pinnable repository file for the layer exists on main and inventing one would repeat the stale-pin failure Spec 040's gate record documents. The occurrence floor of 5 is confirmed at the freeze (DD-055-12). Carried from the draft text: execution likewise stops if the source document cannot be produced from the program's held copy with the §1 material located verbatim; before step 2 it stops if the strict-corpus layer cannot be identified, if the layer cannot be pinned, if the identified sign is absent from it, if the sign is below the frozen occurrence floor of 5.
falsification_tests: each gate's check is itself the test: the execution record must show every gate's verdict in order before the first identification wording or measure, or the run is non-compliant on its face

metadata.strongest_rival: gate-skipping under the pressure of an interesting fragment, with the failure rationalised afterwards
metadata.verdict_rule: the run's own record is the judge: gate verdicts precede outcomes in it, in order, or the outcome is a closure by construction

claims.text: No match under Spec 055 is made by sign number.
claims.boundary: The trap is named in advance from the registry as held today: a W900 value inside a wells_ids cell on the P154 row neither identifies this fragment's sign nor excludes it. claims.text: The behaviour test of spec §5 is specified only for the identified case.
claims.boundary: No behaviour quantity exists for an unidentified sign, an absent sign, or a sign below the floor; the wordings for those cases are §5.4's identification and gate wordings, not behaviour wordings. The pre-counting record (both reference sets, with sources) precedes the first measure in the run order. Ruled at the freeze (DD-055-16): execution requires a worked dry-run of the §5 measures and mapping on a sign other than the target, proving the machinery before it touches the identified sign; the dry-run produces no target quantity and is recorded in the pre-counting record. Carried from the draft text: it runs only on a sign identified under F055-C06, represented in the pinned corpus layer at or above the occurrence floor; its reference sets, measures, outcome mapping are fixed before any measure is computed.
falsification_tests: the run record either shows identification, gate 0.4, and the pre-counting record before the first measure, in that order, or the run is non-compliant on its face

metadata.strongest_rival: counting first and designing the comparison around the counts the run happens to find
metadata.verdict_rule: the ordering is the test: timestamps and record order in the execution's own products decide compliance

evidence.description: Design D-15 (PR #195 packet, §D-15, read in full at this draft): the two-stage falsifier, the identification success/failure conditions, the three measures and criteria, the strict-corpus data statement, and the not-six limit.

claims.text: The known-numeral reference set is fixed from published identifications before counting.
claims.boundary: Excluding the target is what keeps the test a test: the target's published identification is the claim under test, and a set containing it would let the claim stock its own reference range and its own adjacency counts. Ruled at the freeze (DD-055-14): a member whose published identification is hedged in its source is recorded as hedged in the pre-counting record and does NOT enter the known-numeral set for any range, median, or adjacency computation; hedged candidates are listed separately in that record. Carried from the draft text: each member carries its published source, its identifier in the pinned corpus layer; the target sign is not a member of the set; adjacency to another occurrence of the target does not count as numeral adjacency.
alternatives: including sign 900 in the numeral set because its source calls it a special numerical sign (refused: that is the proposition under test)
falsification_tests: the pre-counting record either lists the set with a published source per member and no target membership, or the behaviour stage is non-compliant before it begins

metadata.strongest_rival: circularity by construction: a reference range the target helped define will tend to contain the target
metadata.verdict_rule: set membership is judged from the pre-counting record alone, which is produced before any measure exists

claims.text: The control set is frequency-matched ordinary signs selected by the fixed rule of spec §5.1.
claims.boundary: The rule is this draft's operational form of the design's 'frequency-matched ordinary-sign control set', which names no matching rule (DD-055-6). It is deterministic from the pinned layer's frequency table and the target's census count, both recorded in the pre-counting record; the rule is confirmed at the freeze (DD-055-11) and no rule may be chosen after any §5.2 measure exists. Carried from the draft text: members of neither the numeral set nor the target; the 10 ordinary signs whose occurrence counts in the pinned layer are closest to the target's count, ties broken by corpus identifier in ascending order, all ordinary signs if fewer than 10 exist.
falsification_tests: recompute the selection from the pinned layer's recorded frequency table: a control set not derivable from the target's count by this rule falsifies the pre-counting record

metadata.strongest_rival: a control set chosen for convenience — or for the outcome it produces — after the target's behaviour is already visible
metadata.verdict_rule: the selection is mechanical from recorded inputs; any reader can re-derive the set from the pre-counting record

evidence.description: Design D-15 (PR #195 packet, §D-15, read in full at this draft): the two-stage falsifier, the identification success/failure conditions, the three measures and criteria, the strict-corpus data statement, and the not-six limit.

claims.text: The behaviour outcome is assigned by the mapping of spec §5.3 alone.
claims.boundary: The three measures, the range and median constructions, and the mapping are design D-15's, with two operational forms confirmed at the freeze: 'outside the control set's median' read directionally (DD-055-6; DD-055-11), and positional entropy as Shannon entropy in bits over positions as stored, computed identically for every sign compared (DD-055-15). The mapping is total: every measure pattern lands in exactly one outcome, including the overlap pattern both-sides-on-two, which is MIXED. Carried from the draft text: NUMERAL-LIKE iff the target is numeral-side on at least two measures, control-side on fewer than two; NOT NUMERAL-LIKE iff it is control-side on at least two, numeral-side on fewer than two; MIXED otherwise. Carried from the 0.7-draft head text: the outcome is exactly one of NUMERAL-LIKE, NOT NUMERAL-LIKE, or MIXED.
falsification_tests: the outcome word must be derivable from the published per-measure table by this mapping alone; a word that is not, falsifies the outcome record

metadata.strongest_rival: post-hoc measure-shopping or wording-shopping once the target's numbers are known
metadata.verdict_rule: the per-measure table is published with the outcome; the mapping is recomputed from it by any reader

claims.text: Every terminal outcome of an execution is recorded in one of the pre-written wordings of spec §5.4.
claims.boundary: The wording set covers the full outcome set of spec §11. IDENTIFICATION FAILED and the gate wordings are outcomes of the design, written before any result exists, and carry the same prominence as a behaviour verdict (§8). Filling a bracket with a quantity not present in the run record falsifies the outcome record. Carried from the draft text: NUMERAL-LIKE, NOT NUMERAL-LIKE, MIXED, IDENTIFICATION FAILED, IDENTIFIED — TOO FEW OCCURRENCES TO TEST, CLOSED AT STEP 0, with the bracketed material filled from the run, no other headline wording substituted.
falsification_tests: headline inspection: an outcome record whose headline matches no §5.4 form, or whose filled quantities are absent from the run record, falsifies compliance

metadata.strongest_rival: softened wording after a disappointing outcome — the failure mode the pre-written forms exist to prevent
metadata.verdict_rule: the forms are frozen in this register before execution; the outcome's first paragraph must instantiate exactly one of them

evidence.description: Design D-15 (PR #195 packet, §D-15, read in full at this draft): the two-stage falsifier, the identification success/failure conditions, the three measures and criteria, the strict-corpus data statement, and the not-six limit.

claims.text: No outcome under Spec 055 establishes that the identified sign's value is six.
claims.boundary: Also excluded by this boundary, and stated wherever an outcome is stated: any conclusion about what the sign meant in use beyond the numeral question, and any decipherment claim. Distributional behaviour can support 'this sign is a numeral'; the exact value needs evidence of a different kind (counted depictions, bilingual material) that this program does not hold — design D-15's own limit. Carried from the draft text: the source document's own argument for six is preserved in the recovery record as source material, never cited as evidence at the behaviour stage.
alternatives: quoting the source's tablet equations or its summary sentence as corroboration for a NUMERAL-LIKE outcome (refused: the recovery preserves the argument; the test does not adopt it)
falsification_tests: inspection of every Spec 055 output: a value, meaning, or decipherment claim in any output — or a citation of the source's derivation as behaviour-stage evidence — falsifies compliance and is corrected by dated addendum, never by silent edit

metadata.strongest_rival: the reading in which a numeral-like result plus the source's own argument together amount to the value six being established
metadata.verdict_rule: outputs are judged against this boundary at execution close; violations are recorded defects, and the claim consequence is limited to the identification and behaviour statements of F055-C01
